reason: The hypothesis relies on the formation and strengthening effect of nano-scale B2 NiTi precipitates, but the cited evidence (E4, E5) only discusses B2 NiAl and L12 precipitates in completely different alloy systems (AlCoCrFeNi, Fe-Al-Ni-based). No evidence is provided for the existence, stability, or strengthening effect of NiTi precipitates in the proposed Ti-Ni-Fe-Co-Cr system at 700–900°C. The cited evidence is therefore misrepresented and does not support the key premises.
premises: Equiatomic Ti–Ni-based HEAs can be rendered as a single-phase solid solution
Aging at ~750°C will produce a uniform dispersion of nano-scale B2-ordered NiTi precipitates in this alloy
Nano-scale B2 precipitates act as dislocation pinning centers and impede grain-boundary sliding at 700–900°C
This precipitation strengthening will enhance yield strength and creep resistance without unacceptable ductility loss
The cited evidence (E4, E5) demonstrates B2 precipitate strengthening in other HEA systems
